newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Downtrodden Australian dlr tries tentative rally.
newsitem.headline: Downtrodden Australian dlr tries tentative rally.

text.p: The Australian dollar edged cautiously higher at the midsession in what dealers termed a technical reaction to a deeply oversold position.

Analysts detected some tentative signs a short term bottom may have formed at Wednesday's US$0.7310 low, but emphasised that offers around US$0.7380 needed to be cleared to have any confidence in the rally. A break promised to see US$0.7430 reached in a hurry given how short much of the market was.
The prospects for would-be buyers were bolstered by short covering against the yen triggered by Japanese trade data which showed a far smaller rise in the trade surplus than feared.

Analysts noted exports growth had slowed to 12.5 percent in June from 20.5 percent the month before, while imports growth picked up to 8.7 percent from May's 6.0 percent. This suggested the impact of the April hike in consumption tax was fading, albeit slowly.
The market assumed this would at least help prevent a flare-up in trade friction between Japan and the U.S. and took the U.S. dollar up to 116.00/05 yen from 115.50/55.
Elsewhere on the crosses the A$ recouped some lost ground on its Canadian counterpart following options related demand overnight and talk of fund switching from CAD to AUD bonds.
The local unit shifted to C$1.0123/34 from a weak C$1.0080/90 late here Wednesday, when it had briefly touched a fresh 18-month low around of C$1.0025.

The A$ is still down over six cents on the Canadian currency since May, reflecting the diverging courses of monetary policy in the two countries. The latter hiked rates last month while the market strongly suspects the Reserve Bank will ease official rates soon for the fifth time this cycle.
Many feel it could move as soon as next Friday after consumer price and wages data which are expected to confirm the very benign outlook for inflation. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
